title: Spot the mismatch
header_line: My analysis of one book on neuro-linguistic programming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: Do their words and their actions agree?
A student said: I figure out someone's intentions and see if their behaviors line up; that is where I psychologically begin.
Another said that when they are very vague in telling a story, cannot give details that add up and stutter, you can read them.
I said: you want to detect incongruence. People with a limiting belief and negative language inside do not necessarily expose it; they come with a game face.
I said that when you know what matters to the person, such as that they love children's education, you have a massive advantage in connecting, together with the conversation in person.

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write someone whose words and actions disagree.
Write what else could explain it.
Write the question you would ask.
Write what you know about their values.

check.q: What did a student say to check?
choices: Whether intentions and behaviors line up

check.q: What did I say people come with?
What did I say gives an advantage?

recap: Look for incongruence, then ask. Know what matters to them.
